messages:
rachel: Heads up: infra changed header from X-Route-Policy -> X-Routing-Policy earlier. We're seeing a small but steady stream of 400s coming from older client libs. Anyone tracking SDK work?

tom: Saw it too. Proxy logs show 'missing header X-Routing-Policy' for a subset of requests. Looks like Go and TS clients impacted more.

priya: I rolled a tiny hotfix in the ingress to accept both headers but that's a bandaid. Need SDK patches and a plan to avoid ledger double-counting.

ben: Agreed. Short plan: (1) server canonicalization to a single ledger key, (2) SDK patches to send new header by default but accept legacy, (3) console tile to show migration progress.

rachel: For canonicalization: can we map both header inputs to ledger key format `routing_policy::v1::<value>` before quota write? That should ensure single attribution.

ben: Yes. We'll implement a normalizer middleware in the edge proxy that computes canonical_key and writes that to the request context. Ledger will use canonical_key.

priya: Middleware patch ready in feature branch. It tags request.ctx['routing_policy_key'] and sets migration_tag=legacy|new|both. Need SDKs to emit same tag so console and alerts match.

qa: TS client behavior note: streaming client lowercases header names in one path; new header was dropped. Patch will need to preserve original-case header map or perform case-insensitive checks against known keys.

ben: SDK responsibilities: 1) accept both headers when reading from environment or upstream; 2) when constructing requests, prefer X-Routing-Policy; 3) expose env var RW_ROUTE_HEADER_LEGACY to force legacy for customers; 4) emit telemetry event `route_header_migration` with new/legacy/both.

rachel: Add log line `route_header=legacy source=sdk` when falling back so we can alert customers still on old header.

priya: For rollout: infra accepts both headers immediately. SDKs ship patch as patch/minor. Console tile will be behind a feature flag. Canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h if metrics stable.

qa: I'll add unit tests for streaming (proto frames) and a integration that sends both headers in one request to confirm we tag `both`.

tom: Need to be careful with sampling: console tile needs 100% sampling for migration dimension for accurate %, but global metrics can be 1% to save retention. Analytics OK with that tradeoff?

ben: Yes. Console backend can request full-resolution for tenants when showing the tile; global rollup uses sampled telemetry. We'll implement a tag to indicate sampled/un-sampled events.

rachel: Ops note: reconciler job to merge legacy keys into canonical key for historical data. Start with last 30 days. If mismatch >0.5% open incident.

ops-bot: Scheduled job created: `reconcile-routing-keys` nightly, starting 2026-03-24. Owners: ben, linda.

priya: One more gotcha: private deployments may not pick up SDK patches quickly. We should include migration instructions in customer notice and provide RW_ROUTE_HEADER_LEGACY env var in deployment docs.

rachel: I'll draft the customer email targeted at dedicated/private customers with rollback steps and how to set RW_ROUTE_HEADER_LEGACY.

ben: For end-to-end tests, I'll add a local proxy in CI that asserts ledger sees canonical_key regardless of which header was sent. Also add an e2e that sends both headers to confirm tag `both`.

qa: CI results: quick run shows py client + go client tests pass. TS flaky streaming test failing due to header-case handling. I'll open a fix PR.

tom: Can we include a temporary compatibility layer in the public API docs noting header change and migration steps? Avoid surprises.

rachel: Yes. Docs patch will include example curl, SDK upgrade notes, and env var usage.

priya: Timeline proposal:
- T+0: accept both headers at edge (done)
- T+1: release SDK patches (py/go/ts) + docs + customer notice
- T+2: start 5% canary for console tile and monitor metrics
- T+3..T+4: expand canary to 25/100% if errors <0.1% and reconciler delta <0.5%

ben: I'll own reconciler and ledger canonicalization. qa owns streaming fixes. tom owns docs + CI checks. rachel will own customer comms. priya owns the infra middleware.

ops-bot: Deploy window reserved: 04:00 UTC tomorrow for middleware and proxy change.

rachel: Thanks. Please drop PR links here when ready and I'll track customer comms.

qa: PRs: ts-sdk#402, go-sdk#118, py-sdk#989 (working on tests).

priya: Middleware branch: infra/routing-normalizer#77. Canary flags toggled via infra UI under feature-flags/routing-header-migration.

ben: I'll start the reconciler job draft and post runbook. If we hit unexpected ledger deltas, escalate to #incidents.

rachel: OK closing for now, will re-open if anything spikes.
